article.title: Why Lower Cost per Transaction Can Hide Higher Total Cost
article.why: Separates unit efficiency from total system spending, a common source of budgeting mistakes.
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
Businesses often celebrate a falling cost per transaction. If processing one order used to cost $5 and now costs $3, the operation appears more efficient. But a lower unit cost does not always mean the company is spending less overall. Total cost can rise when transaction volume grows faster than unit cost falls.

Suppose a digital service handles one million transactions at $5 each. Total processing cost is $5 million. After automation, cost per transaction falls to $3. If volume stays at one million, the company saves $2 million. But if lower prices, faster service, or new use cases increase volume to three million transactions, total processing cost becomes $9 million. The unit economics improved while the total bill increased.

This distinction matters in cloud computing, payments, logistics, customer support, and AI. Efficiency can make an activity cheap enough to use more frequently. A company that automates customer support may decide to analyze every conversation instead of a small sample. A cheaper payment channel may attract many more small transactions. The result can be higher total consumption of the resource.

Managers therefore need to separate unit cost, volume, and total cost. Looking at only one of these metrics can produce the wrong conclusion. A finance team may expect savings because unit cost falls, while the operating team plans a major expansion in usage. Both forecasts can be internally correct but inconsistent with each other.

Fixed and variable costs should also be separated. A new platform may require a large fixed investment but reduce the variable cost of each transaction. During the early period, total cost may rise even though long-run economics improve. The payback depends on how quickly volume grows and whether the new capacity is actually used.

Another issue is cost shifting. Automation may reduce labor cost in one department while increasing software, data, monitoring, or support cost elsewhere. If the measurement boundary is too narrow, the organization may report savings that simply moved to another budget.

Quality must be considered too. A lower cost per case is not a true improvement if error rates rise, customers contact support again, or employees spend extra time correcting automated output. Rework should be included in the economic calculation.

A practical cost bridge starts with the old total cost, then shows the effect of lower unit cost, higher or lower volume, new fixed costs, and any costs shifted to other teams. This makes it possible to explain why a successful efficiency program may still require a larger budget.

The same framework helps with planning. Instead of assuming that a 30 percent reduction in unit cost produces a 30 percent reduction in spending, managers can model several volume scenarios. What if usage stays flat? What if it doubles? What if new demand appears because the service becomes cheaper?

Efficiency is valuable because it allows more output from each unit of resource. But ‘more efficient’ and ‘less expensive in total’ are not synonyms. Good management tracks both unit economics and system-level spending.

Volume growth can also change supplier pricing. Some contracts become cheaper per unit at higher volume, while others include step-up charges, premium support, or infrastructure tiers. The relationship between volume and cost is therefore not always linear. Finance should model the actual contract structure rather than multiply a single unit price by expected volume.

Managers should also compare cost with value created. If total cost rises from $5 million to $9 million but the larger transaction volume generates $20 million of additional contribution margin, the higher bill may be economically attractive. Cost control should not become a goal that blocks profitable scale.

The key question is therefore not, ‘Did cost per transaction fall?’ It is, ‘How did efficiency change the economics of the whole system?’ That requires a view of unit cost, demand response, fixed investment, quality, and incremental value together.
paragraphs.zh:
企業常會慶祝 cost per transaction 下降。例如每筆訂單處理成本從5美元降到3美元，看起來效率明顯提升。但單位成本下降，不代表總支出一定下降；如果 transaction volume 增加得比 unit cost 降得更快，total cost 反而可能上升。

假設一個 digital service 原本處理100萬筆交易，每筆5美元，總成本500萬。自動化後每筆降到3美元，如果 volume 不變，確實省200萬；但如果低價格、速度提升或新 use case 讓 volume 增到300萬筆，總成本就變成900萬。Unit economics 改善了，total bill 卻增加。

這在 cloud computing、payment、logistics、customer support 和 AI 都很常見。效率提高會讓某些活動便宜到可以更頻繁使用。

因此管理者要把 unit cost、volume、total cost 分開看。只看其中一個，很容易得到錯誤結論。Finance 可能因 unit cost 下跌而預期節省，但 operation team 同時正在規劃大幅增加 usage。

Fixed cost 與 variable cost 也要拆開。新平台可能需要較大的前期固定投資，但每筆 transaction 的 variable cost 更低。初期總成本可能先上升，長期經濟性才改善。

還要看 cost shifting。自動化可能降低某部門的人力成本，卻增加 software、data、monitoring 或 support 成本。

Quality 也不能忽略。如果 cost per case 下降，但 error rate 上升、客戶重複聯絡，或員工花更多時間修正自動化輸出，就不能稱為真正改善。Rework 也要算進去。

實務上可以做 cost bridge：從舊 total cost 出發，拆出 unit cost 下降、volume 變化、新 fixed cost，以及移到其他部門的成本。

規劃時也不要直接假設 unit cost 降30%，總支出就降30%。可以做多個 volume scenario：usage 不變、翻倍、或因成本下降而出現新需求。

Volume 也可能改變 supplier pricing。有的 contract 在大量使用時 unit price 更低，也有 step-up charge、premium support 或 infrastructure tier，因此成本未必線性。

最後要把 cost 和 value 一起看。若 total cost 從500萬升到900萬，但額外 volume 帶來2,000萬 contribution margin，增加支出可能仍然很划算。

所以真正問題不是『每筆成本有沒有下降』，而是『效率如何改變整個 system 的 economics』。
paragraphs.ja:
businessはcost per transactionの低下を喜びます。しかしunit costが下がってもtotal costが下がるとは限りません。volumeがunit costの低下以上に増えれば総支出は増えます。

1 million transactionsを1件5ドルで処理するとtotal costは5 million dollarsです。automationで3ドルになりvolumeが同じなら2 million節約できます。しかしvolumeが3 millionへ増えればtotal costは9 millionになります。unit economicsは改善してもtotal billは増えます。

cloud、payment、logistics、customer support、AIなどではefficiencyがusageを増やすことがあります。

そのためunit cost、volume、total costを分けて見ます。Financeはsavingを期待していてもoperation teamがusage expansionを計画しているなら、両方のforecastを統合する必要があります。

fixed costとvariable costも分けます。新platformはlarge fixed investmentが必要でもtransaction当たりvariable costを下げることがあります。

cost shiftingにも注意します。labor costが下がってもsoftware、data、monitoring、supportへcostが移っただけかもしれません。

qualityも含めます。error rate、repeat contact、reworkが増えるならlower cost per caseは本当の改善ではありません。

cost bridgeではold total costからunit cost effect、volume effect、new fixed cost、他teamへ移ったcostを分解します。

planningではunit costが30%下がったからspendingも30%下がると仮定せず、flat、double、新需要など複数volume scenarioを試します。

volumeによってsupplier pricingが変わる場合もあります。discountだけでなくstep-up chargeやpremium supportがあるためlinearではありません。

さらにcostだけでなくcreated valueを比較します。total costが5から9 millionへ上がってもadditional contribution marginが20 millionなら経済的に魅力的です。

『more efficient』と『less expensive in total』は同義ではありません。unit economicsとsystem-level spendingの両方を見る必要があります。

vocabulary.usage: Unit cost can fall while total cost rises.
Volume may grow after efficiency improves.
The platform requires a fixed cost.
Rework should be included in the calculation.
Higher cost may still create more contribution margin.
